events.title: ANSI C standard ratified (X3.159-1989)
events.summary: ANSI ratified X3.159-1989 on December 14, 1989 — the first official standard for the C programming language.
events.about: ANSI C (C89/C90) added function prototypes, `const`, and a standard library — so C code could compile the same way on Unix, Windows, and embedded targets. Every modern C compiler still targets this baseline plus later revisions (C99, C11, C17).

narrative.whyChosen: K&R C was informal; ANSI C gave the industry a contract for portable systems code.
narrative.whyImportant: It locked in prototypes and library semantics that made C the lingua franca of OS kernels, drivers, and runtimes.
narrative.problemSolved: Vendors extended K&R C differently; teams needed one normative definition to write code that moved between platforms.
